1.title: Network Monitoring Technologies
1.text: Welcome to Module thirteen: Network Monitoring Technologies. It covers the exam area three point zero Network Operations. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. three point two Given a scenario, use network monitoring technologies: methods (S N M P with traps, M I B, versions and community strings, flow data, packet capture, baseline metrics and anomaly alerting, log aggregation with sys log and sim, A P I integration, port mirroring). Solutions (network discovery, traffic analysis, performance, availability and configuration monitoring). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: three point zero Network Operations (nineteen percent). Exam format: up to ninety questions in ninety minutes; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred passes. Validated against: the official Comp T I A Network plus N ten to nine exam objectives, version four point zero.

1.title: SNMP
1.text: S N M P. Simple Network Management Protocol (S N M P) monitors and manages devices. A manager (N M S) talks to agents on devices. M I B (management information base). The database of values an agent exposes, each with an object identifier (O I D). Polling (get). The manager asks for values (U D P one hundred sixty-one). Trap. The agent sends an alert on its own when an event occurs (U D P one hundred sixty-two). v one or version two C. Community strings (like passwords) sent in clear text. version three. Authentication and encryption, user-based security: use this.

1.title: SNMP, continued
1.text: S N M P. The figure shows this: An S N M P manager polling agents, and an agent sending a trap. Exam tip: S N M P version three is the secure version. Default community strings (public, private) must be changed or disabled.

1.title: Other monitoring methods
1.text: Other monitoring methods. Flow data (net flow, I P fix). Summaries of conversations: who talks to whom, how much, on which ports; traffic analysis. Packet capture. Full packet contents for deep troubleshooting (Wireshark, tcpdump). Baseline metrics. Normal levels of utilization, latency, errors; deviations trigger anomaly alerting and notifications. Log aggregation. Collect logs in one place: sys log collector; a sim (security information and event management) correlates events and alerts. A P I integration. Tools pull data and trigger actions programmatically. Port mirroring (S P A N). The switch copies traffic from a port or V L A N to another port where an analyzer or I D S listens.

1.title: Monitoring solutions
1.text: Monitoring solutions. Network discovery. Finds devices, ad hoc (on demand) or scheduled. Traffic analysis. Who uses the bandwidth (flow data). Performance monitoring. C P U, memory, bandwidth, latency, errors. Availability monitoring. Is it up? (ping, service checks, uptime). Configuration monitoring. Detects changes against the baseline. Exam tip: "See the full contents of traffic" equals packet capture. "See who is using the bandwidth, with little data" equals flow data. "Send a copy of traffic to an I D S" equals port mirroring. Exam tip: Traps are sent by the agent; polls are asked by the manager; S N M P version three is the secure version.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. An administrator wants a switch to send an unsolicited alert when a link fails. Which S N M P feature fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A trap. Traps are alerts sent by the agent.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A security team wants the most secure S N M P version with authentication and encryption. Which should be used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: S N M P version three. S N M P version three adds authentication and encryption.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. An engineer needs to know which hosts consume the most bandwidth without capturing every packet. What fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Flow data. Flow data summarizes conversations and volume.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. An I D S must inspect a copy of all traffic from one switch port. What should be configured? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Port mirroring. Port mirroring copies traffic to an analyzer.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A team wants logs from all devices stored centrally and correlated for security events. Which solution fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A sim with sys log collection. S I E Ms aggregate and correlate logs.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Utilization suddenly doubles compared with normal. Which practice helps notice this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Baseline metrics with anomaly alerting. Baselines make abnormal behavior visible.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which ports does S N M P use? Answer: U D P one hundred sixty-one for queries and one hundred sixty-two for traps. Question two. What does a M I B contain? Answer: The values (O I Ds) an S N M P agent exposes. Question three. What is the difference between S N M P version two C and version three? Answer: version two C uses clear-text community strings; version three adds authentication and encryption.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is net flow an example of? Answer: Flow data. Question five. What does a sim do? Answer: Aggregates and correlates logs and alerts on events. Question six. What does port mirroring do? Answer: Copies traffic from one port to another for analysis.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. S N M P: manager and agent; M I B; get (one hundred sixty-one); traps (one hundred sixty-two); version three secure, version two C community strings. Methods: flow data (summaries), packet capture (full), baselines, sys log plus sim, A P I, port mirroring. Solutions: discovery (ad hoc or scheduled), traffic, performance, availability, configuration monitoring.
